sentences.text: That, the land measuring 20-Kanals under Survey no.654 Min has reference to and is part of Survey No.654 in the last Settlement i.e., 1977 Bikrami.

The Mislihaqiyat of 1977 Bikrami in this regard shows the whole Survey No. 654 measuring 381 Kanals 12 Marlas as Naallah and hence in respect of whole land 381 Kanals and 12 Marlas under the Survey No. 654, LB-6/C is not attracted/applicable.
7. That, the relevant provisions of Govt. Order No.LB-6/C of 1958 are reproduced as under:
1 (c) (iv) "(iv) fail to cultivate the land for more than one year or neglect to conform to standards or cultivation prevalent in the village."
2 (ii) & (iii) "(ii) recorded or used as pathway, grazing ground, graveyard, cremation ground, camping ground, khul (irrigation channel) or forest demarcated or otherwise including Berun line;
(iii) held by any government Department or institution under the control of the Government."
That, in the case in hand, the land in question was not under the continuous cultivating possession of Abdul Qayoom S/o Ghulam Qadir Sheikh w.e.f, Kharif 1957-58.
Said land was also recorded as Gair Mumkin Nallah as per Misalhaqiyat 1977 Bikrami and Banjri Qadeem as per prospective records.

The Govt Order LB-6/C of 1958 dated 05-06-1958 was not applicable in the case, as such,
Mutation No. 1000 (LB-6/C) and Mutation No. 432/C have been attested in clear violation of law/orders governing the subject.
8. That, as per Govt. Order No. S-432 of 1966, the condition laid down for conferring property rights to cultivators of the State land and recorded as tenants-at-will in terms of Govt. Order LB-6 is that the land should be held by the occupant in self cultivation continuously from Kharif 1957-58.

On the contrary, land in question has remained uncultivable for years together since 1957-58 onwards and as a result, the land has been recorded as Banjri Qadeem / Gair Mumkin Nallah in the subsequent records, as such, mutation No.1000 (LB-6) and 1001 (432/C) attested in the year 1997, are legally invalid.

9. Considering the above recorded position and the conditions as laid down vide Standing Order No.23 (A) for the purpose of attestation of Mutation under LB-6/C following inferences and conclusions are drawn:
a) The application for Sehate-e-Kasht was to be rejected by the attesting officer as per para 88 of standing Order No.23 (A) which provides that the land recorded as Gair Mumkin Nallah/Dariya cannot be converted/recorded as any other type of land and therefore, Mutation No.345 (Sehat-e- Kasht) appears to have been attested in contravention to the guidelines provided in Standing Orden Order No.23 (A).

sentences.text: Further perusal of the record tends to show that in so far as order dated 5.8.2015 passed by Deputy Commissioner, Ganderbal, respondent 4 herein is concerned whereby the mutations 1000 and 1001 have been set aside and declared as void ab initio, it is manifest that the said order came to be passed by the respondent 4 herein without any prior notice to the petitioner and in fact the said order came to be passed by Deputy Commissioner Ganderbal, respondent 4 herein suo moto even though no appeal was pending before him against the said mutations.

This court in case titled as "Om Parkash and others vs. Union Territory of J&K and others [WP(C) 2360/2021 clubbed with OWP 549/2019 dated 2.3.2024 has held that the Deputy Commissioner has no authority to set aside a mutation attested by Tehsildar in terms of Government order no. sentences.text: The other reason given by the Deputy Commissioner, Ganderbal, respondent 4 herein, qua the land in question is that the land in question is "Gair Mumkin Nallah".

It may have been true that previously the land falling in survey no. 654 may have been recorded as Nallah, however, the fact as is clearly reflected in the order of the Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, respondent 3 herein, is that in the Jamabandi of 1957-58, 18 kanals of said land has been recorded as "Abi Saum" and the fact that the said land came to be identified for construction of Inspector Bungalow for Police Training School, Manigam and a notification thereof in terms of section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1990 had been issued in this regard is sufficient to suggest that the land in question is not a Nallah as there can be no doubt that if it were a Nallah, it would not have been identified or earmarked for acquisition for raising construction of Inspection Bungalow for Police Training School Manigam.

The whole exercise of Deputy Commissioner Ganderbal, respondent 4 herein seemingly is aimed at depriving the petitioner of the compensation consequent upon the acquisition of the said land and the very premise on the basis of which the Deputy Commissioner, Ganderbal,
respondent 4 herein issued order dated 5.8.2015 apparently appears to be non-existent and actuated by extraneous considerations.
The said order dated 5.8.2015 thus has been rightly set aside by the Appellate Authority Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, respondent 3 herein, upon the appeal filed by the petitioner herein.

A reference in this regard to section 8 of J&K Land Revenue Act, Samvat 1996 becomes necessary, which reads as under:
8. Control. --
(1) The general superintendence and control over all Revenue offices shall be vested with the Government.
(2) The Divisional Commissioner, the Collectors and Assistant Collectors shall be subordinate to and under the control of the Financial Commissioner.
(3) Subject to the control of the Financial Commissioner, the Collectors shall be subordinate to and under the control of a Divisional Commissioner.

A bare perusal of the aforesaid provision makes it manifestly clear that the Collector (Deputy Commissioner) is subject to the control of the Divisional Commissioner and in terms of the provisions of the Land Revenue Act, Samvat 1996, the Divisional Commissioner is prescribed as an Appellate Authority qua the orders passed by the Deputy Commissioner and it does not stand to reason that the Deputy Commissioner shall challenge order of his superior authority as it would be subversive and abuse of process of law.

A reference in this regard to the judgment of the Apex Court passed in case titled as "Gridco Limited vs. Western Electricity Supply Company of Orissa Limited and others" reported in (2024) 2 SCC 500 would be relevant, wherein in para 31 following came to be observed:
"There is one more aspect of the matter.

sentences.text: As held by the Constitution Bench, under Section 62, the Commission exercises quasi-judicial powers.
There are appeals preferred by the Commission against the orders of the Appellate Tribunal in appeals under Section 111 of the Electricity Act.
The Appellate Tribunal in appeals has dealt with the legality and validity of the decisions of the Commission rendered in the exercise of quasi- judicial power.
In short, the Appellate Tribunal has tested the correctness of the orders of the Commission.
The Commission is bound by the orders of the Appellate Tribunal.

Therefore, we have serious doubt about the propriety and legality of the act of the Commission of preferring appeals against the orders of the Appellate Tribunal in appeal by which its own orders have been corrected.
The Commission cannot be the aggrieved party except possibly in one appeal where the issue was about the non- compliance by the Commission of the orders of the Appellate Tribunal......."

9. It is also significant to mention here that the revisional jurisdiction vested in the Financial Commissioner, Revenue, respondent 2 herein under section 15 of the Land Revenue Act, Samvat 1996, can be exercised against an order within a reasonable time and having regard to the fact that basic mutation by virtue of which the petitioner has been recorded as tenant in place of previously recorded tenant stands attested almost six decades back and therefore the same cannot be allowed to be questioned now and that a consequential mutation attested in terms of Government order no.
